record.paper_title: Understanding Solar Flares and Energetic Events: Open questions, observational requirements, and instrumental needs over the coming decade
record.original_question: How do radiation and energetic-particle fluxes from stellar flares affect the habitability of orbiting planets, especially through atmospheric retention, atmospheric erosion or chemistry changes, and changes to surface conditions?

evidence.quote: • How do ﬂare radiation and particle ﬂuxes impact the habitability of orbiting planets, through inﬂuences such as atmospheric retention and surface condition impacts [87, 88]?

artifact.category_tag: stellar flare effects on exoplanet habitability
artifact.status_search_result: This is an active, broadly open research question in astrobiology and stellar-planet interactions. Numerous studies (e.g., Segura et al. 2010, Tilley et al. 2019, Airapetian et al. 2020, Chen et al. 2021) have modeled aspects of flare-driven atmospheric chemistry, ozone depletion, and SEP impacts, but a complete quantitative framework predicting habitability outcomes across the full parameter space remains unresolved, and observational constraints on flare SEDs and SEP fluxes for other stars are limited.

status_evidence.title: Impact of Space Weather on Climate and Habitability of Terrestrial-Type Exoplanets
status_evidence.snippet: Airapetian et al. (2020) review the effects of stellar XUV and SEP fluxes on atmospheric escape and chemistry, identifying numerous open questions.
status_evidence.claim: Quantifying flare and SEP effects on exoplanet habitability remains an open, active research area.

status_evidence.title: Modeling Repeated M Dwarf Flaring at an Earth-like Planet in the Habitable Zone
status_evidence.snippet: Tilley et al. (2019) show repeated flares with SEPs can deplete ozone by orders of magnitude, but full habitability outcomes depend on poorly constrained parameters.
status_evidence.claim: Partial quantitative results exist for ozone depletion, but a complete habitability framework is not yet established.
